Great questions — answered inline below + short examples. Looping in Dev and Neha on the technical caching/edge behavior so they can add any platform nuances.

1) Prompt caching vs billed tokens:
- Billing model (hosted) = billed tokens = model compute used to process the request (input tokens + output tokens). If a request is served entirely from a cache (i.e., no model execution), the compute portion is not billed as model tokens. 
- However, there are two common caching patterns to be aware of:
  a) Prefix/KV cache at the runtime (fast path): if the model is resumed from a KV cache for the same conversation prefix, you still run some compute for the new tokens but benefit from reduced compute for cached prefixes — you are billed for the actual compute performed (so input tokens processed by the model + newly generated output tokens).
  b) Response cache (HTTP-level): if the response is a literal cache hit (exact same request+context) and we return the stored response without invoking the model, you will not be billed for output tokens. There may be a tiny metering entry for the request itself (counted in logs) but it's not charged at the token rate.

2) Tokens vs characters (ballpark):
- For English prose, 1 token ≈ 3–4 characters on average (so 1M tokens ≈ 3–4M characters). Short prompts with lots of punctuation or non-English text change the ratio.

Example calc (using your workbook numbers):
- Average prompt length: 300 characters (~75–100 tokens)
- Average response length: 900 characters (~225–300 tokens)
- So one interaction ≈ 300–400 tokens (input + output).
- If you have 2M interactions/month at that size → ≈ 600–800M tokens/month. At $20 / 1M tokens, that would be $12k–$16k/month in token spend.

3) Target $/1M tokens = $20?
- $20 / 1M tokens is in the achievable range for some model families on Hosted for production if you:
  • use smaller/faster model variants for lower-cost paths where quality is acceptable,
  • enable prefix/KV caching for repeated conversational prefixes, and
  • use batching and autoscaling appropriately (or Dedicated reserved capacity which reduces per-token cost at high volume).
- For high-quality Llama-family or bigger open models, typical hosted list prices are higher; Dedicated reserved capacity and quantized runtimes can get your effective cost down substantially vs list. We can run a concrete scenario in the workbook and show Hosted vs Dedicated spend.

Quick technical confirmation from the runtime side:
- Response cache hits: we return the cached payload without invoking the model runtime. Those hits do not incur token charges. We still emit a log/metric event (for metrics and rate-limits) but no token billing line.
- Prefix/KV cache: when the runtime resumes from KV, the model still executes to condition on the previous context; you are billed for the tokens the model actually processes during that execution. That cost is typically lower than reprocessing the entire prefix but not zero.
- Metering nuances: our billing pipeline counts tokens consumed by model execution. We also show request counts in the Console for traffic analysis (useful for concurrency planning) but requests are not directly token-billed.

If you want, I can add a column in the workbook showing: raw chars → token estimate → billed tokens under (a) no cache, (b) prefix/KV hit, (c) response-cache hit. That makes the billable delta very explicit.
